apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-attested-wasm
spec:
  rules:
  - name: attestation-check
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
        selector:
          matchLabels:
            app: wasm-edge

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design progressive delivery gates at scale, with multi-cloud constraints and real-world SLO-based rollouts; focuses on policy, tooling (Argo Rollouts, Prometheus), and CI integration; evaluates trade-offs between safety and speed, failure modes; ensures observability and reproducibility.

## Key Concepts

- Progressive delivery with Argo Rollouts Canary
- AnalysisTemplate and Prometheus metrics
- Promotion rules based on consecutive analyses and SLO breach thresholds
- CI gates validating manifest shape and rollout strategy
- Rollback/promotion semantics in production

## Code Example

```yaml
# AnalysisTemplate (Prometheus-based)
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: AnalysisTemplate
metadata:
  name: canary-analysis
spec:
  metrics:
  - name: error-rate
    successCondition: result < 0.01
    failureCondition: result >= 0.05
    provider:
      prometheus:
        address: http://prometheus-operated.default.svc.cluster.local
        query: avg(rate(http_requests_total{status!~"2.."}[5m]))
```

```yaml
# Minimal Rollout using Canary
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Rollout
metadata:
  name: myservice
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: myservice
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: myservice
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: myregistry/myservice:canary
  strategy:
    canary:
      analysis:
        templates:
        - templateName: canary-analysis
      stepWeight: 20
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test for promotion failure modes if the AnalysisTemplate temporarily becomes unavailable?
- How would you adapt this gate for multi-tenant environments with separate SLIs per tenant?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Question Is Asked
This tests practical policy design, edge-case handling, and CI integration for Kubernetes manifests in a multi-team environment. Candidates must demonstrate understanding of resource isolation, pod hardening, network security, and hardware scheduling constraints.

## Key Concepts
- **ResourceQuota and LimitRange**: Prevent resource starvation and enforce default resource requests/limits per namespace
- **Pod securityContext**: Enforce runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, and capability dropping for workload hardening
- **Ingress TLS with cert-manager**: Ensure encrypted external traffic with automated certificate management
- **GPU scheduling constraints**: Use nodeSelector and resource requests to restrict GPU workloads to approved namespaces and nodes
- **CI validation**: Integrate Kyverno/OPA Gatekeeper with kubectl dry-run for pre-merge enforcement

## Code Example
```yaml
# Kyverno ClusterPolicy for ML Platform Gates
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: enforce-ml-platform-gates
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
    - name: require-resource-quota
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Namespace]
      validate:
        message: "Each namespace must have a ResourceQuota."
        pattern:
          metadata:
            annotations:
              quota-ready: "true"

    - name: require-security-context
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Pod]
      validate:
        message: "Containers must run as non-root with read-only filesystem and drop ALL capabilities."
        pattern:
          spec:
            containers:
              - securityContext:
                  runAsNonRoot: true
                  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
                  capabilities:
                    drop: [ALL]

    - name: require-ingress-tls
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Ingress]
      validate:
        message: "Ingress must use TLS with cert-manager annotation."
        pattern:
          metadata:
            annotations:
              (cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer): "?*"
          spec:
            tls:
              - secretName: "?*"

    - name: gpu-in-approved-namespaces
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Pod]
      preconditions:
        - key: "nvidia.com/gpu"
          operator: In
          value: ["1", "2", "4"]
      validate:
        message: "GPU pods are only allowed in approved namespaces with nvidia nodeSelector."
        pattern:
          spec:
            nodeSelector:
              nvidia.com/gpu: "?*"
```

## Verification Strategy

**Local Testing:**
```bash
# Install Kyverno
kubectl apply -f policy.yaml

# Dry-run validate manifests
kubectl apply --dry-run=server -f manifest.yaml

# Test policy against sample manifests
kyverno apply policy.yaml --manifest manifest.yaml
```

**CI Integration (GitHub Actions):**
```yaml
name: Manifest Validation
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Validate with Kyverno
        run: |
          kyverno apply cluster-policy.yaml \
            --manifest manifests/ \
            --policy-report \
            --fail-only-on-exists
```

## Why This Question Is Asked
This question evaluates the ability to integrate image provenance with runtime governance in a GPU-driven, multi-tenant Kubernetes environment. It spans CI pipelines, admission controls, and cross-system attestations—core skills for securing production ML platforms.

## Key Concepts
- **Image Provenance**: Using cosign and Rekor to cryptographically verify container image origins
- **SBOM Signing and Verification**: Ensuring software bills of materials are tamper-proof and traceable
- **Central Provenance Store**: A single source of truth for validated digest information
- **Admission Constraints**: Kyverno/OPA policies enforcing GPU type and quota at deploy time

## Code Example
```yaml
# GitHub Actions: Sign, generate SBOM, and attest
name: Gate: image provenance
on: [push]
env:
  REGISTRY: ghcr.io
  IMAGE_NAME: ${{ github.repository }}
  SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.COSIGN_KEY }}

jobs:
  build-sign-attest:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Build and push image
        run: |
          docker build -t ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }} .
          docker push ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }}
      - name: Install cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v3
      - name: Sign image with cosign
        run: |
          cosign sign --yes --key ${{ env.SIGNING_KEY }} \
            ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }}
      - name: Generate and sign SBOM
        run: |
          syft ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }} -o spdx-json=sbom.json
          cosign attest --yes --key ${{ env.SIGNING_KEY }} \
            --type sbom \
            ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }}
      - name: Upload to Rekor (automatic with cosign attest)
        run: |
          echo "Rekor entry created automatically during attestation"
      - name: Store central provenance digest
        run: |
          DIGEST=$(docker inspect ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }} \
            --format='{{index .RepoDigests 0}}')
          echo "${{ github.sha }}:$DIGEST" >> provenance_store.txt
```

```yaml
# Kyverno admission policy
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: image-provenance-gate
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  rules:
    - name: verify-image-digest
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Deployment]
      verifyImages:
        - imageReferences:
            - "ghcr.io/*"
          attestors:
            - entries:
                - keyless:
                    subject: "https://github.com/org/*"
                    issuer: "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
          verifyDigest: true
          required: true
    - name: enforce-gpu-type
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Deployment]
      context:
        - name: namespace
          apiCall:
            urlPath: /api/v1/namespaces/{{ request.namespace }}
      preconditions:
        - key: "{{ request.namespace }}"
          operator: NotEquals
          value: "kube-system"
      validate:
        message: "GPU type must match namespace label"
        pattern:
          spec:
            template:
              spec:
                containers:
                  - (resources.limits."nvidia.com/gpu"): "?*"
    - name: enforce-gpu-quota
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Deployment]
      validate:
        message: "GPU quota exceeded for namespace"
        deny: |
          {{ exists request.namespace.metadata.labels."gpu-quota" }}
```

```yaml
# Minimal GitHub Actions workflow
name: Helm Security Gate
on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - 'charts/**'
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - uses: actions/setup-helm@v3
      - name: Render and validate security context
        run: |
          helm template myapp charts/myapp > rendered.yaml
          # Validate security context fields

```

```python
# scripts/validate-security.py
import sys, yaml
with open(sys.argv[1]) as f:
    docs = yaml.safe_load_all(f)
for doc in docs:
    if doc.get('kind') == 'Deployment':
        for container in doc['spec']['template']['spec']['containers']:
            ctx = container.get('securityContext', {})
            if not ctx.get('runAsNonRoot'):
                print(f"FAIL: {container['name']} missing runAsNonRoot")
                sys.exit(1)
            if not ctx.get('runAsUser', 0) >= 1000:
                print(f"FAIL: {container['name']} runAsUser < 1000")
                sys.exit(1)
            if not ctx.get('readOnlyRootFilesystem'):
                print(f"FAIL: {container['name']} missing readOnlyRootFilesystem")
                sys.exit(1)
print("All security context checks passed")
```

  name: myapp
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:

        image: nginx:latest

          runAsUser: 1000

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to implement SBOM-based attestations and runtime provenance checks, plus how to wire CI gates with Kosign and CycloneDX.

## Key Concepts

- Image provenance, cosign signatures, attestations
- CycloneDX SBOMs, embedded in image annotations
- GitHub Actions gating, runtime enforcement (Kyverno/OPA)

## Code Example

```yaml
name: prod-provenance
on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - manifests/prod/**
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: setup cosign
        run: |
          curl -sSfL https://github.com/sigstore/cosign/releases/download/v1.10.0/cosign-linux-amd64 -o cosign
          chmod +x cosign
          sudo mv cosign /usr/local/bin/
      - name: verify images
        run: |
          cosign verify -key cosign.pub registry.example.com/namespace/service:tag
      - name: verify SBOM attestation
        run: |
          cyclone_dx_attest --image registry.example.com/namespace/service:tag --attest
```

- How would you handle attestation revocation and key rotation?
- How to scale SBOM checks across many services and environments?
